ei.title: There’s More than One Way to Vote
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: We make many personal choices in our lives, from who to have lunch with to what career to pursue. However, there are many situations where we must make decisions as a group. Group decision-making is not as simple as our personal choices, as it involves numerous voices with differing opinions. Voting is often used to make group decisions fairer and more efficient, and various voting methods have been developed over time. The following story illustrates how these different voting methods work. The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide how to raise money for children in need. Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions. So they decided to put it to a vote. When they asked for advice from Ms. Akers, the council’s advisor, she encouraged them not to use the familiar voting method, but to try something different instead. After doing some research, the council members decided to try three different voting systems: the first-past-the-post (FPTP) method, the alternative vote (AV) method, and the Condorcet method. The entire council was curious to find out if the different methods would yield different results. On the day of the vote, each possible event was given a letter: “art show” was represented by the letter A, the letter B indicated “bake sale,” and C stood for “charity concert.” Each of the 20 council members was given a voting slip and instructed to write down the options in order of preference. For example, if the charity concert was their first choice, followed by the bake sale and the art show, they would write CBA. After every member had voted, the voting slips were counted. The results were as follows: The First-Past-The-Post Method The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods. Voters are given several options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes wins. Neither the second nor third preference matters at all, so they are ignored. This method is commonly used in political elections around the world. The student council quickly determined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert. This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7. The FPTP method is uncomplicated and easy to understand, but it has a significant weakness. It is possible to win a vote without the support of the majority. That was the case here. According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was to hold a charity concert. However, only 8 out of 20 council members chose the charity concert as their first preference, which equaled 40% of the total votes. The Alternative Vote Method Next, the council members examined the votes using the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result. The AV method can potentially include more than one round of counting. For an option to win in the first round, it needs to get more than 50% of the first-preference votes. As the charity concert only received 40% of the total votes, a second round of counting was required. Option A, the art show, received the fewest first-preference votes, with only 5 council members voting for it. Therefore, option A was eliminated, and the 5 council members’ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences. As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were added to the total. This meant that option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9. As a result, the bake sale would be the winner. Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either. It sometimes allows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes. In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received. The Condorcet Method Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. This method involves comparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options. In this case, there were three pairs to consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C. Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, voting either ABC, ACB, or CAB. Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA. Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9. They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9. As option A, the art show, was preferred to both of the other options, it would be considered the winner. The Condorcet method’s weakness is that, along with being complex, it sometimes fails to select a winner. This is especially true in elections that contain numerous options. It is possible that no option will be clearly preferred over the others. Instead of all methods pointing toward a single option and making the council’s choice easier, the winner differed with each method. After a long, intense discussion with Ms. Akers, the student council members decided to choose the Condorcet method, as they liked the idea of directly comparing each option with the others. Everyone agreed that they learned a lot about different voting systems through this experience. It is obvious that choosing an ideal voting method is a complex and challenging task. No voting system is flawless or clearly superior to another. Whichever we choose will have pros and cons. Some people believe that it is best to keep the process simple by not ranking our choices at all. Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting, arguing that more complex methods deliver more accurate results. All of these efforts are designed not to make decision-making difficult and inefficient, but to help us make better decisions as a society. Ultimately, understanding all of the possible voting methods and weighing their pros and cons allows us to better understand the process of decision-making. When we understand decision-making better, we are more likely to become better decision-makers ourselves.

questions.passage: The results were as follows: The First-Past-The-Post Method The FPTP method is the (A)[simplest / hardest] of the three methods. Voters are given several options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes wins. Neither the second nor third preference matters at all, so they are (B)[ignored / counted]. This method is (C)[commonly / rarely] used in political elections around the world. The student council quickly determined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert. This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7. The FPTP method is uncomplicated and easy to understand, but it has a significant weakness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① simplest(가장 단순한)+ignored(무시되는)+commonly(흔히): FPTP가 세 방법 중 '가장 단순하고', 2·3순위는 '무시되며', 이 방법이 정치 선거에서 '흔히' 쓰인다는 문맥에 모두 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ② hardest(가장 어려운)는 '가장 단순한' 방법이라는 설명과 정반대
❌ ③ counted(집계되는)는 2·3순위가 '무시된다'는 흐름과 반대
❌ ④ rarely(드물게)는 정치 선거에서 '흔히' 쓰인다는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: simplest=가장 단순한, ignored=무시되는, commonly=흔히

Option A, the art show, received the (B)[fewest / most] first-preference votes, with only 5 council members voting for it. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① definitely(확실히)는 '~할 수도 있다(can)'는 가능성 표현과 어울리지 않음
✅ ② potentially(잠재적으로)+fewest(가장 적은)+eliminated(탈락된): AV 방식은 한 번 이상의 집계를 '가능성 있게' 포함하고, 최소 득표한 A안이 '가장 적은' 표를 받아 '탈락'했다는 문맥에 맞음 ← 정답
❌ ③ most(가장 많은)는 5표로 최소 득표한 상황과 반대
❌ ④ selected(선택된)는 표가 적어 '탈락'했다는 흐름과 반대
det.tip: potentially=잠재적으로, fewest=가장 적은, eliminated=탈락된

questions.passage: It is obvious that choosing an ideal voting method is a complex and challenging task. No voting system is flawless or clearly (A)[superior / inferior] to another. Whichever we choose will have pros and cons. Some people believe that it is best to keep the process simple by not ranking our choices at all. Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting, arguing that more complex methods deliver more (B)[accurate / misleading] results. All of these efforts are designed not to make decision-making difficult and inefficient, but to help us make (C)[better / worse] decisions as a society. Ultimately, understanding all of the possible voting methods and weighing their pros and cons allows us to better understand the process of decision-making. When we understand decision-making better, we are more likely to become better decision-makers ourselves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① inferior(열등한)는 어떤 방식도 다른 것보다 '우월하지' 않다는 문맥과 반대
❌ ② misleading(오해를 부르는)은 복잡한 방식이 더 '정확한' 결과를 준다는 주장과 반대
❌ ③ worse(더 나쁜)는 더 '나은' 결정을 돕는다는 글의 결론과 반대
✅ ④ superior(우월한)+accurate(정확한)+better(더 나은): 완벽하거나 명백히 '우월한' 제도는 없고, 복잡한 방식이 더 '정확한' 결과를 준다고 주장하며, 이 모든 노력이 더 '나은' 결정을 돕는다는 문맥에 맞음 ← 정답
det.tip: superior=우월한, accurate=정확한, better=더 나은

questions.passage: The FPTP method is uncomplicated and ①<u>easy</u> to understand, but it has a ②<u>significant</u> weakness.  It is possible to win a vote without the support of the ③<u>minority</u>.  That was the case here.  According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was to hold a charity concert.  However, only 8 out of 20 council members ④<u>chose</u> the charity concert as their first preference, which equaled 40% of the total votes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ minority → majority: 다수(majority)의 지지 없이도 이길 수 있다
det.analysis:
✅ ① easy: FPTP가 복잡하지 않고 이해하기 '쉽다'는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② significant: 하지만 '중대한' 약점이 있다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ minority(소수) → majority(다수): FPTP의 약점은 '다수의 지지 없이도' 이길 수 있다는 것이므로 majority가 맞다. minority는 정반대 ← 정답
✅ ④ chose: 20명 중 8명만 자선 콘서트를 1순위로 '선택했다'는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: majority(다수) ↔ minority(소수)

det.korean: ② matching → conflicting: 의견이 '서로 충돌해서(conflicting)' 투표에 부침
det.analysis:

det.analysis:
❌ ① counting(집계): 표가 '더 큰 집계'를 갖는다는 것은 어색하고 표의 힘을 나타내지 못함
❌ ② support(지지): 2순위 표가 1순위 표보다 더 큰 '지지'를 갖는다는 것은 문맥과 맞지 않음
✅ ③ influence(영향력): AV 방식은 때때로 2순위 표가 1순위 표보다 더 큰 '영향력'을 갖게 한다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답

❌ ② distant: 멀리 있는 (관련 없음)

❌ ④ equal: 동등한 (관련 없음)
det.tip: flawless(흠 없는, 완벽한) ↔ faulty(결함 있는)

questions.passage:
(A) The AV method sometimes needs more than one <u>round</u> of counting before a final winner is chosen. If no option gets a majority at first, another one is held.
(B) The children sat around a big <u>round</u> table and shared their snacks. Its smooth surface had no sharp corners at all.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 round의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② (A) round of counting은 집계를 다시 하는 '(진행) 회차·차례'를 뜻하고, (B) round table은 모서리 없는 '둥근' 탁자를 뜻함 ← 정답
❌ ① (A)는 '둥근'이 아니라 집계 회차
❌ ③ (A)는 '공격'이 아니라 집계 회차
❌ ④ (B)는 '소란'이 아니라 둥근 모양
det.tip: round: (A) (반복되는) 회차 / (B) 둥근

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a person who gives official advice and help to a group or organization"

det.analysis:
✅ ① advisor: 어떤 집단이나 조직에 공식적인 조언과 도움을 주는 사람 ← 정답
❌ ② voter: 투표하는 사람(유권자)
❌ ③ winner: 이긴 사람이나 선택지
❌ ④ method: 방법, 방식
det.tip: the council's advisor = 학생회 조언자 → advisor = 조언과 도움을 주는 사람

questions.passage: Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. This method involves __________ (compare) the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: compare(동사 원형) → comparing(동명사): 동사 involve는 뒤에 목적어로 동명사(-ing)를 취한다. involve comparing(비교하는 것을 포함하다)이 맞으므로 comparing으로 바꿔야 한다.
det.tip: involve + 동명사(-ing): involves comparing(비교하는 것을 포함하다)

questions.passage: Ultimately, understanding all of the possible voting methods and __________ (weigh) their pros and cons allows us to better understand the process of decision-making. When we understand decision-making better, we are more likely to become better decision-makers ourselves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: weigh(동사 원형) → weighing(동명사): 문장의 주어가 'understanding ... and ___ ...'로, 앞의 동명사 understanding과 and로 나란히 이어지는 자리다. 같은 형태(동명사)로 맞춰야 하므로 weighing이 맞다.
det.tip: understanding ... and weighing ...: and로 이어지는 병렬은 같은 형태(동명사)로

questions.passage: It is obvious that choosing an ideal voting method is a complex and challenging task.  No voting system is flawless or clearly superior to another.  Whichever we choose will have pros and cons.  Some people believe that it is best to keep the process simple by not ranking our choices at all.  Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting, arguing that more complex methods deliver more accurate results.  All of these efforts are designed not to make decision-making difficult and inefficient, but to help us make __________ as a society.  Ultimately, understanding all of the possible voting methods and weighing their pros and cons allows us to better understand the process of decision-making.  When we understand decision-making better, we are more likely to become better decision-makers ourselves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① louder voices(더 큰 목소리): 의사결정을 돕는다는 흐름과 무관
❌ ② larger profits(더 큰 이익): 이익이 아니라 결정의 질에 관한 글
❌ ③ faster results(더 빠른 결과): 속도가 아니라 더 나은 결정이 핵심
✅ ④ better decisions(더 나은 결정): 이 모든 노력은 의사결정을 어렵게 만들려는 게 아니라 사회로서 '더 나은 결정'을 하도록 돕기 위한 것이라는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
det.tip: help us make better decisions as a society: 사회로서 더 나은 결정을 하도록 돕다

questions.passage: The Condorcet method’s weakness is that, along with being complex, it sometimes __________.  This is especially true in elections that contain numerous options.  It is possible that no option will be clearly preferred over the others.  Instead of all methods pointing toward a single option and making the council’s choice easier, the winner differed with each method.  After a long, intense discussion with Ms.  Akers, the student council members decided to choose the Condorcet method, as they liked the idea of directly comparing each option with the others.  Everyone agreed that they learned a lot about different voting systems through this experience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 fails to select a winner(승자를 정하지 못한다)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① counts every vote twice(모든 표를 두 번 센다): 뒤에 이어지는 '어떤 안도 명백히 선호되지 않을 수 있다'는 흐름과 무관
❌ ② ignores the first preference(1순위를 무시한다): Condorcet 방식의 약점 설명과 맞지 않음
✅ ③ fails to select a winner(승자를 정하지 못한다): 뒤 문장에서 '선택지가 많은 선거에서 특히 그렇고, 어떤 안도 명백히 선호되지 않을 수 있다'고 하므로, 이 방식이 때때로 '승자를 뽑지 못한다'는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
❌ ④ changes the final result(최종 결과를 바꾼다): 승자를 못 정하는 약점과 다른 내용
det.tip: no option will be clearly preferred(어떤 안도 명백히 선호되지 않음)라는 단서 → fails to select a winner
